title: peek_requests.moderation_status defaults to 'pending' while the live contract requires 'approved', so any insert path omitting it strands the request invisibly

impact: A Peek Request created by any path that does not explicitly set moderation_status is invisible to the public thread and cannot be accepted by the seller — it strands with no error surfaced to the buyer. The safe default is the one the MVP contract requires, not the legacy moderation default.

title: MFA is enforced only in the browser; no assurance-level check exists in any policy, function or trigger, so an aal1 token reaches every admin RPC directly
location: src/App.jsx:115-132,147-151; src/services/authService.js:159-165; supabase/migrations (all 159 — zero matches for aal1/aal2/assurance/amr); supabase/migrations/0088_private_authorization_helper_implementations.sql
evidence: useMfaGate calls authService.mfaChallengeRequired(), which reads currentLevel/nextLevel client-side and returns a boolean used only to choose which React component to render. Grepping all migrations for aal1, aal2, assurance and amr returns no matches. private.is_admin() tests role membership only. Supabase exposes the level in SQL as auth.jwt() ->> 'aal', so the control is available and unused.
impact: MFA provides no protection against API access, which is the threat it is deployed for. An attacker who compromises an admin password signs in, receives a valid aal1 session, is shown the MFA challenge screen, and simply does not use the SPA — calling PostgREST and the admin RPCs directly with the aal1 bearer token. Every server-side check passes because none require aal2. Admin capability covers user suspension and ban, listing and service takedown, Peek removal, conversation action and verified-business decisions.
reproduction: Sign in as an MFA-enrolled admin, stop at the challenge screen, take the access token from the session and call an admin RPC directly against /rest/v1/rpc/ — it succeeds
root_cause: MFA added as a client-side route gate without a corresponding database-side assurance-level predicate
recommended_fix: Require auth.jwt() ->> 'aal' = 'aal2' inside private.is_admin() and private.is_super_admin() for accounts holding a verified factor, or add an aal2 predicate to admin RLS policies and the prelude of every admin RPC
test_to_prove_fix: pgTAP asserting an admin RPC called with an aal1 JWT is denied while the same call with aal2 succeeds
notes: Appendix C gate 'MFA cannot be route-bypassed' = FAIL. Precondition is prior credential compromise, which is why this is rated P1 rather than P0; treat as P0 if MFA is the compensating control for admin password compromise.

title: Search mixes keyset cursor pagination with an offset range() path

impact: Offset pagination is unstable under concurrent inserts: a listing published while a buyer pages can push results down so an item is shown twice or skipped entirely. Inconsistent with the cursor strategy used elsewhere.

root_cause: Two pagination strategies introduced at different times and not reconciled
recommended_fix: Move the remaining offset path onto the cursor RPC
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting no duplicate or skipped row across a page boundary when a row is inserted mid-scan
notes: Primary search path already uses the correct strategy

title: Sellers cannot mark a listing sold; the only terminal action is unavailable
evidence: owner_transition_listing restricts p_action to ('submit','pause','resume','unavailable'). The listing_status enum contains 'sold', 'rented' and 'under_offer', but no migration or client path writes them: grepping for set status/next_status to 'sold' returns nothing.
impact: A marketplace cannot record the outcome that matters most. Sold and withdrawn collapse into one state, so buyers lose the signal that an asset actually transacted, sellers cannot close a listing honestly, and the product loses its only free measure of whether it is working. For property and vehicles, a stale live listing that was actually sold is also a direct trust problem.
reproduction: Open /my-listings and look for a sold action — only pause, resume and unavailable exist
root_cause: Status vocabulary defined in v1 but the transition RPC was scoped to publication states only
recommended_fix: Add a 'sold' (and 'rented' for rentals) action to owner_transition_listing with the matching UI affordance and public treatment
test_to_prove_fix: pgTAP asserting an owner can transition available -> sold and that sold listings leave public search
notes: under_offer and rented are equally unreachable

title: The seller's new-Peek-Request notification deep-links to the buyer page and there is no top-level seller queue route
evidence: The alert inserted for the listing owner sets link '/peek-requests'. App.jsx:191 routes /peek-requests to BuyerPeekRequests, the buyer-side page. No route resolves to a seller fulfilment queue; the seller components are BuyerPeekRequestsQueue and ResponsePeekBindingQueue, reached from elsewhere.
impact: A seller notified of a buyer's Peek Request follows the link and may land on a page that does not show the request. This is the entry point of the product's core differentiating journey, so a dead-ending deep link here breaks the loop at its most fragile moment.
reproduction: Trigger a Peek Request against a listing you own on another account, then follow the notification link as the seller
root_cause: Notification link written before the seller queue had its own route
recommended_fix: Add a dedicated seller queue route and point the owner alert at it
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting the owner alert link resolves to a route that renders the seller fulfilment queue
notes: The underlying accept_peek_request authorization is correct; this is routing only

title: Messaging has no realtime transport and no refetch on focus or reconnect, so new messages can go unseen
evidence: @supabase/realtime-js is aliased to a stub that throws if .channel() is ever called, and Realtime is disabled in supabase/config.toml. query-client.js sets staleTime 30 minutes, gcTime 1 hour, refetchOnWindowFocus false and refetchOnReconnect false.
impact: A buyer or seller can sit on an open conversation and not see a reply until they navigate. In a market where WhatsApp is the competing channel and connectivity is intermittent, silent message latency pushes users off-platform, which also defeats the contact-privacy boundary the product works hard to maintain.
reproduction: Send a message from a second account and observe the first client without navigating
root_cause: Realtime deliberately removed for bundle size and cost; polling or focus-refetch was not substituted
recommended_fix: Enable refetchOnWindowFocus and refetchOnReconnect for conversation queries, or add interval polling on the active thread, or restore Realtime for messaging only
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting an inbound message appears within a bounded interval without manual navigation
notes: Stubbing Realtime is a defensible bundle decision; the gap is that nothing replaced it

title: No evidence of EXIF/GPS stripping on listing images, which defeats the deliberate coordinate coarsening
evidence: 0049 deliberately separates public_latitude/public_longitude from exact coordinates held in listing_private_locations, but no strip or re-encode step for still-image EXIF was found in the upload functions or migrations. The Peek video pipeline produces derivatives, implying re-encode, but the still path does not.
impact: A listing photo taken on a phone commonly embeds GPS coordinates accurate to a few metres. Anyone can download a public listing image and read the exact location of an occupied home, defeating the coarsening control entirely. The brief identifies exact occupied-property coordinates as a physical-safety risk.
reproduction: Upload a geotagged photo to a listing, fetch the public image URL and read its EXIF
root_cause: Location coarsening implemented at the database layer without a matching media-layer control
recommended_fix: Strip all EXIF on upload, or re-encode images server-side, and add a test asserting no GPS tags survive
test_to_prove_fix: Test uploading a known-geotagged fixture and asserting the served object contains no GPS EXIF
notes: Marked LIKELY rather than CONFIRMED: absence of a strip step is evidenced, presence of GPS in served objects needs a hosted check

title: The Turnstile Edge Function is deployed but never invoked from the frontend
evidence: The Edge Function exists and reads TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY, TURNSTILE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS and TURNSTILE_ALLOWED_HOSTNAMES, but grepping all of src/ for turnstile returns nothing. No signup, listing creation, contact reveal or report flow presents a challenge.
impact: Account creation is free and unchallenged, which is the multiplier that turns the per-account contact-reveal cap into an ineffective control (F-035). Spam listing and report floods are likewise limited only by per-account SQL rate limits.
reproduction: Search src/ for any Turnstile widget or token submission — there is none
root_cause: Server-side verification built first; the client integration was never completed
recommended_fix: Wire the Turnstile widget into signup at minimum, and into contact reveal and reporting, passing the token to the existing Edge Function
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting signup without a valid Turnstile token is rejected
notes: The server half is already written, so this is an integration gap rather than new work

title: The contact-reveal cap is per account while account creation is unprotected, so scraping scales linearly with free accounts
evidence: v_limit constant integer := 40 counted against contact_reveal_events within interval '24 hours', scoped to the calling user.
impact: 0109's own header calls contact harvesting the primary real-world abuse target for a classifieds marketplace. With free unchallenged signup (F-034), 25 accounts yield 1,000 seller contacts per day entirely within policy. contact_reveal_events records the harvest after the fact rather than preventing it.
reproduction: Create several accounts and reveal 40 contacts on each within 24 hours
root_cause: Cap correctly scoped per identity, but identity is cheap to mint
recommended_fix: Add Turnstile to signup (F-034), and add a second cap keyed on IP or device alongside the per-account cap; consider alerting on reveal-rate anomalies in contact_reveal_events
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting reveals are throttled across multiple accounts originating from one source
notes: The per-account cap and audit trail are correct as far as they go

title: Price sorting and range filtering compare raw numbers across currencies with no normalised sort key
evidence: listings.price numeric(14,2) with currency as a sibling column and no normalised column such as price_usd written at submission. featureFlags.currencyConversion defaults false. exchange_rates exists but is not applied to search ordering.
impact: A price-ascending sort or a price-range filter over a mixed-currency result set ranks 500 in one currency against 500 in another, so buyers see a false ordering and cheap-looking listings that are not cheap. In a market where currency choice is itself meaningful, this is a trust problem rather than a cosmetic one.
reproduction: Post two listings at the same numeric price in different currencies and sort by price ascending
root_cause: Currency modelled correctly per row but never normalised for comparison
recommended_fix: Write a normalised sort key at submission using exchange_rates, or scope result sets to a single currency per country context and label sorts accordingly
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting a mixed-currency result set orders by normalised value, or that the UI prevents mixed-currency ordering
notes: Money typing and per-row currency are otherwise correct

title: 'Current evidence' wording implies a recency the pipeline does not attest
evidence: The manifest describes the product as letting buyers 'request current evidence before you commit'. The pipeline validates and transcodes the video but does not verify capture time, and no freshness indicator or capture timestamp was found on the playback surface.
impact: A seller can upload footage recorded months earlier and it presents identically to footage recorded today. Since the product's differentiator is current visual evidence, an unattested recency claim is the one place the product risks overclaiming.
reproduction: Upload an old video file as a Response Peek and observe that nothing marks its age
root_cause: Recency is a product promise without a corresponding technical control
recommended_fix: Either capture and display a server-side received-at timestamp with clear wording, or soften the claim to 'recent evidence supplied by the seller'
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting the playback surface renders a received-at timestamp
notes: The rest of the product's trust copy is accurate and does not overclaim

title: No duplicate or stolen-media detection against the highest-frequency fraud pattern in property and vehicle marketplaces
evidence: Media validation proves the uploader owns the storage object but says nothing about image provenance. No perceptual hash, no cross-listing image comparison and no reverse-image check exists anywhere in the repository.
impact: Recycled photography is the most common real-world scam in property and vehicle classifieds: copy images from a genuine listing, advertise below market, collect viewing fees or deposits. The product's central promise is visual evidence, so failing here undermines the proposition directly. Peeks are the partial answer, being harder to fake than stills, but Peeks are unreachable in production (F-003), so at launch listings carry only unverifiable stills.
reproduction: Post a listing using images copied from another live listing — accepted without objection
root_cause: Media pipeline scoped to ownership and format validation, not provenance
recommended_fix: Add perceptual hashing (pHash) at upload and flag or block cross-listing collisions for review; prioritise property and vehicles
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting a second listing reusing an existing listing's image is flagged
notes: Report-driven takedown remains the only current mitigation

title: Reduced-motion support is near-absent and the mask-icon colour is inconsistent with the brand direction
evidence: Only 2 prefers-reduced-motion declarations across a UI using animate-spin, transitions and an immersive Peek video player. index.html sets theme_color #050914 and color-scheme dark while mask-icon colour is #2563EB blue.
impact: Users with vestibular sensitivity get no motion relief on the most animated surface in the product. The colour inconsistency is cosmetic.
reproduction: Enable reduce-motion at OS level and open the Peek player
root_cause: Motion added per component without a global reduced-motion strategy
recommended_fix: Add a global prefers-reduced-motion rule disabling non-essential animation; reconcile mask-icon colour with the brand palette
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting animation classes are suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion
notes: Accessibility investment is otherwise well above typical

title: Initial JS of roughly 178 KB gzip is heavy for the mid-range-Android and 3G target
evidence: Measured build: 1,507,014 bytes JS across 151 chunks; index + App + BrandLogo shared chunk is about 594 KB raw and 178 KB gzip. verify-build-budget.mjs passes, so this is within the declared budget.
impact: On a 400 kbps effective connection this is roughly 3.5 to 4 seconds of transfer before any content renders, before parse and execute on a low-end device. The stated market is mobile-first with constrained data.
reproduction: Build and measure the entry chunks
root_cause: Shell imports more than it needs; vendor chunking was measured and correctly rejected as a worse trade
recommended_fix: Reduce what the app shell imports rather than re-chunking; audit the 200 KB shared chunk for shell-only dependencies
test_to_prove_fix: Budget gate tightened with a per-route first-load ceiling
notes: Declared budget gate is green; this is budget tightening not a violation

title: The public listing projection ships full descriptions to card and search views
evidence: The 35-column anon allowlist includes description (validated up to 5,000 characters), variants and photos jsonb. Card and search rendering needs title, price, location label and a thumbnail.
impact: A 20-card search page can carry roughly 100 KB of description text that is never rendered. On constrained mobile data this is pure waste on the most-used screen.
reproduction: Inspect a search response payload against what the card renders
root_cause: One projection serves both card and detail reads
recommended_fix: Add a narrower card projection RPC or column subset for list views
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting the card query response omits description
notes: Column allowlist is otherwise correct and privacy-preserving

title: No evidence of server-side image derivatives or srcset for listing stills
evidence: listing_upload_intents records mime_type and byte_size but no derivative generation was found for still images, and no srcset/sizes attributes were located. The Peek pipeline does produce 720p derivatives and webp thumbnails.
impact: Grids likely serve full-size camera uploads, which on 3G is the single largest avoidable cost on the discovery surface.
reproduction: Inspect the served URL for a listing thumbnail and compare against the original upload size
root_cause: Derivative pipeline built for Peek video but not for listing stills
recommended_fix: Generate and serve width-appropriate derivatives with srcset for listing images
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting a grid image request returns a derivative smaller than the original
notes: Corroborated by failing test 22 which asserts images declare loading and decoding behaviour

title: No per-route metadata, OG tags or prerendering, so every shared listing produces an identical blank preview
location: index.html; src/ (no document.title, no helmet, no meta management); vite.config.js
evidence: index.html contains zero og: or twitter: tags. No document.title assignment, metadata library or SSR/prerender step exists anywhere. Every route serves the same static head.
impact: Sharing a listing to WhatsApp — identified in the brief as a major contact channel in this market — produces a generic card with no title, price, location or photo, for every listing. Google sees every listing as a duplicate of the shell with no title, description or canonical. No structured data is emitted.
reproduction: Fetch /property/<id> with curl and inspect the head; or paste a listing URL into WhatsApp
root_cause: Client-only SPA shipped without a metadata strategy
recommended_fix: Add per-route metadata (title, description, canonical, OG, Twitter) and prerender or server-render listing routes so unfurlers and crawlers receive real content
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting a listing route serves a title and og:image matching the listing
notes: src/lib/share.js exists but sharing a URL with no metadata still yields a blank preview

title: No sitemap.xml exists or is referenced
evidence: robots.txt is well written and correctly scoped but declares no Sitemap: directive, and no sitemap file exists.
impact: With no per-page metadata and no sitemap, discovery of individual listings depends entirely on crawler JS rendering plus internal linking.
reproduction: ls public/ and grep robots.txt for Sitemap
root_cause: Not yet implemented
recommended_fix: Generate a sitemap from published listings and reference it from robots.txt
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting sitemap.xml exists and lists published listings

title: Listing URLs are bare UUIDs with no slug and removed listings return HTTP 200
evidence: Routes are /property/:id, /car/:id, /machinery/:id where :id is a UUID. The SPA rewrite returns index.html with HTTP 200 for every path, so a removed listing renders PageNotFound under a 200 status.
impact: Unreadable, unshareable URLs in text contexts, and search engines are never told a removed listing is gone.
reproduction: Share a listing URL as plain text; request a deleted listing and inspect the status code
root_cause: Client-only routing with no slug strategy or status differentiation
recommended_fix: Add slugs to listing URLs and serve real 404/410 status for removed listings via prerendering
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting a removed listing URL returns 404 or 410

title: No frontend error reporting exists, so browser failures are invisible to operators
location: package.json; src/ (no sentry or equivalent); vite.config.js:54-57
evidence: Neither package.json nor any file in src references Sentry or any error-reporting SDK. The only production visibility is 4 console.error call sites deliberately retained.
impact: A render error, a bootstrap failure, a post-deploy chunk-load failure, or a failed Peek upload on a seller's phone produces no signal to the operator. Breakage is learned only from user reports, and for a marketplace launching into intermittent connectivity that is the majority of real failures.
reproduction: Trigger any client error and observe that nothing is recorded anywhere
root_cause: Error reporting deferred; console.error retained as the interim measure
recommended_fix: Add a frontend error reporter with authenticated source-map upload, wired to AppErrorBoundary, the bootstrap catch and the upload paths
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting a thrown render error produces a reporter call
notes: Server-side and database observability is by contrast thorough

title: No product analytics, so none of the four critical funnels is measurable for drop-off
evidence: No analytics SDK or event pipeline exists. The only analytics hits are AdminRecommendationAnalytics.jsx, an internal admin view over recommendation_* tables.
impact: Server tables allow post-hoc reconstruction of outcomes but not drop-off. There is no way to learn whether sellers abandon at media upload or at contact entry, which is the single most valuable thing a pre-launch marketplace can measure.
reproduction: Search src for any event-tracking call
root_cause: Analytics deferred
recommended_fix: Instrument the buyer and seller funnels, or record an explicit accepted-gap decision
test_to_prove_fix: Funnel events asserted present for create-listing start, media, validate and publish
notes: The brief permits an explicitly accepted gap here; the point is to decide consciously

title: No self-service data export; requests are manual with no documented process or SLA
evidence: The override copy states self-service export is not yet available and export requests are handled through support. Deletion by contrast is fully implemented via the delete-account Edge Function and account_deletion_receipts.
impact: Data subject access requests depend on an undocumented manual process with no stated timeframe, on a service that collects identity documents and a selfie for business verification.
reproduction: Attempt data export from Settings — only deletion is offered
root_cause: Deletion prioritised and shipped; export deferred
recommended_fix: Implement self-service export, or document the manual process with an SLA and an owner
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting an export request produces a complete archive of the account's personal data
notes: REQUIRES PROFESSIONAL REVIEW for statutory response timeframes

title: Obsolete tests assert a removed Peek moderation step and the old brand, contradicting current product decisions and each other
evidence: Failing test 508 asserts the seller queue 'waits for moderation before answering', a step the MVP removed. Failing test 34 asserts 'the polished FindIt identity is present across app shells and install metadata', directly contradicting tests/peekaListingBrandContracts.test.mjs which asserts FindIt absence.
impact: The suite encodes superseded product decisions, so it cannot go green without deleting contradictory assertions. Two brand tests now assert opposite things, which means any attempt to fix the suite forces a product decision that should be explicit.
reproduction: node --test ./tests/*.test.mjs and read the failures
root_cause: Tests retained across an MVP boundary change and a rebrand without reconciliation
recommended_fix: Delete or rewrite tests asserting removed moderation and the old brand; keep one authoritative brand contract
test_to_prove_fix: Suite green on main with a single authoritative brand assertion
notes: Also corroborates F-017, F-029 and F-042 from the repository's own tests

title: 83 percent of test files assert on source strings rather than behaviour
location: tests/ (117 of 141 files use readFile with assert.match)
evidence: Counted across tests/*.test.mjs and tests/security/*.test.mjs: 117 files read source text and match against it; 24 import and exercise behaviour.
impact: Source-string tests verify that code looks a certain way, not that it works. A suite that is 83 percent string matching cannot substantiate a release-certification claim, and F-002 shows the failure mode concretely.
reproduction: Count readFile usage across the test suite
root_cause: Cheap convention pinning scaled up in place of behavioural coverage
recommended_fix: Convert the launch-priority suites to behavioural tests against a real database; keep string tests only for conventions
test_to_prove_fix: Behavioural coverage asserted for the brief's 17 launch priorities

title: No browser or E2E framework, so the highest-value end-to-end journey is never executed
evidence: No browser automation dependency exists. The brief's highest-value journey — signup, create listing, immediate publish, search, detail, contact or Peek request, seller fulfilment, buyer result — is not executed anywhere.
impact: Every cross-boundary integration failure between UI, RPC, RLS, storage and worker can only be found in production.
reproduction: Inspect package.json devDependencies
root_cause: E2E deferred
recommended_fix: Add Playwright and implement the single highest-value journey first
test_to_prove_fix: The full buyer-to-seller journey executing green in CI
notes: Chromium and Playwright are already available in the execution environment

title: Admin Peek queue uses pre-approval vocabulary for what is actually report-driven safety
evidence: The RPC is admin_tour_queue_page with the error string 'We could not load the Peek moderation queue' and the imported action is moderateAdminTour, but the cursors are reportedPriority and failedPriority and the report transition is guarded where moderation_status = 'approved', so it only demotes already-published Peeks.
impact: Reviewers reasonably conclude the MVP still has a pre-publication approval queue when it does not. This audit had to trace three migrations to resolve it.
reproduction: Read the RPC name and error string, then read the actual transition guards
root_cause: Vocabulary retained from the pre-MVP moderation model
recommended_fix: Rename to a report queue vocabulary and update the customer error string
test_to_prove_fix: n/a
notes: Determination: report-driven post-publication safety, which the MVP permits

title: Feature flags are build-time only, so incident response requires a redeploy on a pipeline that is currently red
evidence: All capability flags are VITE_FEATURE_* read from import.meta.env at build time. Tables marketplace_feature_controls and marketplace_operational_controls exist, suggesting a runtime control plane was intended, but the browser flags do not read them.
impact: Disabling a misbehaving capability during an incident requires a full rebuild and redeploy. Deployment workflows are currently failing on main, so the kill switch is unavailable exactly when it would be needed.
reproduction: Attempt to disable a capability without a redeploy
root_cause: Flags implemented as build-time constants
recommended_fix: Read capability state at runtime from marketplace_feature_controls with a build-time default, so a flag can be flipped without a deploy
test_to_prove_fix: Test asserting a runtime control change disables a capability without rebuilding

title: Staging deployment is failing, so the environment the capability model depends on is not being built
evidence: Deploy staging to GitHub Pages shows 0 success and 3 failure plus 1 cancelled across the last 30 runs on main, and fails at ee6f212. resolveStagingCertifiedFlag enables messaging, notifications, Peeks and current-location only in a trusted staging environment.
impact: Peeks, messaging, notifications and current-location can only be exercised in staging, and staging is not being built. So the capabilities gated behind staging certification cannot be certified at all, which blocks the Peek release acceptance that F-003 depends on.
reproduction: Inspect Deploy staging to GitHub Pages runs on main
root_cause: Same skip-cascade root cause as F-013 plus environment configuration
recommended_fix: Fix the gate (F-013), restore staging deployment, then run Peek release acceptance
test_to_prove_fix: A green staging deploy followed by a hosted Peek journey run
notes: Blocks F-003 remediation

title: The Cloudflare edge layer is largely declared but unused and no wrangler.toml is committed
evidence: The Env interface declares LIGHTWEIGHT_JOBS, PLATFORM_CONFIG, RATE_LIMITS, three R2 buckets, MEDIA_DELIVERY_HOST and secrets. Four of these — PLATFORM_CONFIG, RATE_LIMITS, LIGHTWEIGHT_JOBS and MEDIA_DELIVERY_HOST — appear exactly once each in the 187-line file, meaning declaration only. infrastructure/cloudflare contains only .example files.
impact: The repository presents a Cloudflare edge, R2 media and rate-limiting architecture that is not implemented and not provisioned. Live media delivery actually runs through Supabase Storage signed URLs, which the CSP confirms. Any capacity or cost planning based on the declared architecture would be wrong.
reproduction: Count references to each Env binding in the Worker body
root_cause: Architecture scaffolded ahead of implementation
recommended_fix: Either implement and provision the edge layer or remove the unused bindings and document Supabase Storage as the media path
test_to_prove_fix: Worker integration test exercising each declared binding

title: 59 of 159 migrations have no rollback script
evidence: Directory counts: 159 migrations against 100 rollback scripts.
impact: A migration without a rollback cannot be reversed under incident pressure, so recovery from a bad migration depends on point-in-time restore, which is itself unverified (E-004).
reproduction: Compare the two directory listings
root_cause: Rollback discipline applied to most but not all migrations
recommended_fix: Author rollbacks for the 59 uncovered migrations, or document explicitly which are irreversible and why
test_to_prove_fix: CI check asserting every migration has a paired rollback or a documented exemption
notes: The rollback gate that enforces non-destructive rollbacks is itself currently red (F-013)

title: No evidence of a restore drill and no stated RPO or RTO
evidence: DR documentation exists but no drill record, no restore evidence and no RPO/RTO targets were found anywhere in the repository.
impact: An untested backup is an assumption. Recovery time is unknown, so the business cannot state how much data or time it would lose in an incident.
reproduction: Search the repository for any restore drill record
root_cause: Documentation written; the drill was never performed or never recorded
recommended_fix: Perform a restore into a scratch project, record the timings, and state RPO and RTO
test_to_prove_fix: Documented restore drill with measured RPO and RTO
